column1: # pref defaults fold across ALL pref members even when not the leading entry (regression)
# `top|top` is one value with two spellings, so it must collapse. Go's
# disjunct dedup compared values without a case for top, so the pair
# survived: canon kept both members, and the un-collapsed disjunct then
# hid the fact that a bare unresolved `top` is not generable -- which both
# ports already agree on for a plain `x:top`.
# The preference row is the control: `*top` and `top` are NOT the same
# value, so that pair must NOT collapse.
# A DISJUNCTION THAT RESOLVES TO NULL EMITS null, NOT NOTHING.
# Go's Gen returns (any, error) and so collapses TypeScript's two distinct
# empty results -- undefined (nothing) and null (JSON null) -- into one
# nil, reconstructing the difference from the child Val. That test had no
# case for a disjunct, so `null|top` (which folds to null, since
# `null & top` is null) read as "generated nothing" and the key was
# silently DROPPED -- and a list element with it, which is worse, because
# The members are genuinely different values, so no amount of deduping
# reaches this: it survives the top|top fix entirely.

# unresolved disjunction now refuses too, so the null case is spelled
# with the PREFERENCE that actually decides it. What is being pinned is
